answer: Mechanism, stated concretely: a new identity must burn a bounded amount of compute, roughly one CPU-hour of hash work, before it can earn anything, and every submission stakes part of its balance that reputation-weighted juries can slash. The beacon words fit the design: glacier captures the stake an honest agent locks before speaking, falcon tracks the transparency that makes every pattern visible, and basalt stands for the slashing that punishes duplicate work. An attacker minting N fake identities pays N times that burn up front, then loses each stake a jury rejects.
